reply_text:
I’d fix these before merging. Reviewed `excerpt-helper` at `59856d7` against `main`.

1. **[P1] Text that fits is still truncated and given an ellipsis** — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no length check before finding the last space and appending `…`. `excerpt('hello world', 20)` returns `'hello…'`, even though the entire text fits; empty text returns `'…'`. Return fitting text unchanged, as the README promises.

2. **[P1] The helpers aren’t connected to card rendering** — `src/excerpt.js:5–8`, `src/card.js:1–2`  
   `card()` still returns the full, trimmed body. Neither `excerpt()` nor `toPlain()` has a production caller, and `excerpt()` doesn’t invoke `toPlain()`. A long Markdown body therefore still appears in full with its markup. Wire up the plain-text → excerpt → card path and cover it with an integration test.

3. **[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit is unnecessarily dropped** — `src/words.js:2–3`  
   `slice(0, limit)` excludes the space at index `limit`, so the search falls back to the previous space. `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `'one…'` instead of `'one two…'`. Check whether the limit itself is a word boundary before backing up. The current words test actually locks in this off-by-one behavior.

4. **[P2] Markdown cleanup deletes literal characters too** — `src/plain.js:3`  
   Removing every `_`, `*`, `~`, and backtick treats ordinary content as formatting. For example, `toPlain('snake_case and file_name')` returns `'snakecase and filename'`, even though those intraword underscores are literal Markdown text. Strip formatting constructs rather than deleting these characters globally.

All **4 existing tests pass**, but they don’t catch these cases. No files changed.
